lesson: Today we work on verbs. A verb is an action word. The lesson is that action words do more work than describing words. Look at three spots. The poem says the rooster throws his rusty question. Throws is the action. It does more than calling the rooster loud. The hose drips its slow arithmetic. Drips gives you the sound and the pace. And you'd found the loose thread, followed it, pulled it clean. Three verbs in a row move you through the whole task. This works because a verb shows a thing happening, and your mind pictures the motion right away. You feel the action before you stop to think about it, that keeps the lines moving. Try this, find one describing word in your draft, and replace it with a verb that shows the same thing happening. The second time through, track only the verbs, then hear how so up is one last brush into action.
